'''''Narcissus tazetta''''' ('''paperwhite''', '''bunch-flowered narcissus''', '''bunch-flowered daffodil''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007|accessdate=2014-10-17}}</ref> '''Chinese sacred lily''', '''cream narcissus''', '''joss flower''', '''polyanthus narcissus''') is a [[Perennial plant|perennial]] [[ornamental plant]] that grows from a [[bulb]]. [[Cultivar]]s of ''N. tazetta'' include 'Caniculatus', [[Narcissus 'Grand Soleil d'Or'|'Grand Soleil d'Or']] and 'Ziva', which are popularly used for forcing indoors, as is the form of ''N. tazetta'' known as Chinese Sacred Lily.<ref name="FarrCarter2005">{{cite book|author1=Judith Farr|author2=Louise Carter|title=The Gardens Of Emily Dickinson|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=tK8nnFJ-KxUC&pg=PA252|access-date=25 July 2012|date=31 October 2005|publisher=Harvard University Press|isbn=978-0-674-01829-7|page=252}}</ref><ref name="MartinGarden2000">{{cite book|author1=Tovah Martin|author2=Brooklyn Botanic Garden|title=Old-Fashioned Flowers: Classic Blossoms to Grow in Your Garden|url=https://archive.org/details/isbn_9781889538150|url-access=registration|access-date=28 July 2012|date=1 March 2000|publisher=Brooklyn Botanic Garden|isbn=978-1-889538-15-0|page=[https://archive.org/details/isbn_9781889538150/page/14 14]}}</ref><ref name="Li2002">{{cite book|author=H. L. Li|title=Chinese Flower Arrangement|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=tE-D3NYtGwUC&pg=PA48|access-date=28 July 2012|date=3 December 2002|publisher=Courier Dover Publications|isbn=978-0-486-42316-6|page=48}}</ref>

== Description ==
[[File:Narcissus-tazetta-2014-Zachi-Evenor.jpg|thumb|The mountain [[ecotype]] in Israel.]]
[[File:Narcissus tazetta - Shoam Forest 2021-12-11 IZE-161a.jpg|thumb|Close-up on flowers]]
''Narcissus tazetta'' is amongst the tallest of the narcissi, and can grow to a height of up to {{convert|80|cm}},<ref name=Tazetta/> with thin, flat leaves up to {{convert|40|cm}} long and  {{convert|15|mm}} wide. [[Umbels]] have as many as 8 flowers, white with a yellow corona.<ref>[https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/358309#page/302/mode/1up Linnaeus, Carl von. 1753.  Species Plantarum 1: 290 ''Narcissus tazetta'']</ref><ref>[https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/9873434#page/159/mode/1up Haworth, Adrian Hardy. 1819.  Supplementum Plantarum Succulentarum 142,  ''Hermione tazetta'' ]</ref><ref>[https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/7430515#page/367/mode/1up Rafinesque, Constantine Samuel. 1848.  Flora Telluriana 4: 21 ''Jonquilla tazetta'' ]</ref><ref>[https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/12313177#page/54/mode/1up Rouy, Georges C. Chr. 1912.  Flore de France 13: 40  ''Narcissus linnaeanus'' ]</ref><ref>Sessé y Lacasta, Martín & Mociño, José Mariano. 1894.  Flora Mexicana ed. 2: 85 ''Pancratium tazetta''</ref>

== Taxonomy ==

===Subspecies===
Six subspecies are accepted by the ''World Checklist of Selected Plant Families'':<ref name="WCSP">Search for "Narcissus tazetta", {{Citation |title=World Checklist of Selected Plant Families |publisher=[[Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew]] |url=http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/ |access-date=2012-12-26 }}</ref>

* ''N. tazetta'' subsp. ''aureus'' <small>(Jord. & Fourr.) Baker</small><ref>Baker, John Gilbert. 1888. Handbook of the Amarylldaceae p 9</ref> syn. ''N. bertolonii'' – south-east [[France]], [[Sardinia]], north-west [[Italy]], [[Algeria]], [[Morocco]]
* ''N. tazetta'' subsp. ''canariensis'' <small>(Burb.) Baker</small><ref name="baker8">Baker, John Gilbert. 1888. Handbook of the Amarylldaceae p 8</ref> – [[Canary Islands]]
* ''N. tazetta'' subsp. ''chinensis'' <small>(M.Roem.) Masam. & Yanagih.</small><ref>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=240001489 Flora of China v 24 p 269, ''Narcissus tazetta'' var. ''chinensis'', common name 水仙 shui xian ]</ref><ref>Masamune, Genkei & Yanagihara, Masayuki. 1941.  Transactions of the Natural History Society of Formosa 31: 329.</ref> – south-east [[China]], [[Japan]], [[South Korea]]
* ''N. tazetta'' subsp. ''corcyrensis'' <small>(Herb.) Baker</small><ref>Baker, John Gilbert. 1888. Handbook of the Amarylldaceae p 7</ref> – [[Corfu]] ([[Greece]])
* ''N. tazetta'' subsp. ''italicus'' <small>(Ker Gawl.) Baker</small><ref name="baker8"/> syn. ''N. italicus'' – Mediterranean from southern [[France]] to [[Greece]]
* ''N. tazetta'' subsp. ''tazetta'' – widely distributed from the western [[Mediterranean Basin|Mediterranean]] to [[Afghanistan]]

==Ecology==
''Narcissus tazetta'' contains a fragrant compound found in only a few other plants, including [[Rosa (plant)|roses]] and ''[[Acnistus arborescens]]'', called [[orcinol]] dimethyl ether, which is almost undetectable to the human nose. Experiments with [[honeybees]] have shown they can readily detect it.<ref name="DudarevaPichersky2006">{{cite book|author1=Natalia Dudareva|author2=Eran Pichersky|title=Biology of Floral Scent|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=wd3mlhZGLAMC&pg=PA95|date=27 March 2006|publisher=CRC Press|isbn=978-0-8493-2283-9|page=95}}</ref>

==Distribution==
''Narcissus tazetta'' is a widespread species, native to the [[Mediterranean Basin|Mediterranean]] region from [[Portugal]] to [[Turkey]]. It is also naturalized across the [[Middle East]], [[Central Asia]], [[Iran]], [[Afghanistan]], [[Pakistan]], [[India]], [[Nepal]] and [[Bhutan]], as well as the [[Canary Islands]], [[China]] ([[Fujian]], [[Zhejiang]]), [[Japan]],  [[Australia]], [[Korea]], [[Norfolk Island]], [[New Zealand]], [[Bermuda]], [[Mexico]] and the United States ([[Oregon]], [[California]], [[Texas]], [[Alabama]], [[Arkansas]], [[Florida]], [[Louisiana]], [[Mississippi]], [[North Carolina]], [[South Carolina]], [[Virginia]], and [[West Virginia]])<ref>[http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=282289 Kew Checklist of Selected Plant Families]</ref> and South America.<ref>[http://www.chileflora.com/Florachilena/FloraEnglish/HighResPages/EH1716.htm Chile Flora]</ref>

== Uses ==
''Narcissus tazetta'' is grown commercially for its [[essential oil]], mostly in southern France. An interspecies hybrid, with ''[[Narcissus poeticus]]'', is also grown for its essential oil.<ref name="Groom1997">{{cite book|author=Nigel Groom|title=The New Perfume Handbook|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UYrDPqLVD-kC&pg=PA225|access-date=28 July 2012|date=30 June 1997|publisher=Springer|isbn=978-0-7514-0403-6|pages=225–226}}</ref>
